verdict.rationale: Zep supports user-level and thread-level graphs with strict per-user isolation (zep-docs-19, zep-docs-20), and ABAC/RBAC policies can scope access for agents, API keys, and UserGroups, enabling some cross-agent access control (zep-docs-12, zep-docs-25, zep-docs-38, zep-docs-54). However, there is no explicit documentation of a 'group/team memory' construct that lets multiple agents or users share a designated subset of memory while other memory remains private — UserGroups appear to be an access-control concept rather than a shared-memory pool, and no example shows selective sharing of specific facts/edges across users. Missing for 10: explicit shared/group memory graph feature, documentation of selective cross-user/agent sharing with per-item privacy controls, and independent verification of this multi-tenant sharing behavior in practice.
